DIAGNOSIS READY: Paraneoplastic Pemphigus (associated with underlying malignancy).

The combination of a new onset cough and persistent mucosal changes (specifically ulcers) in a patient with normal inflammatory markers, autoimmune panels, and no response to standard therapies for other bullous diseases strongly suggests paraneoplastic pemphigus. The normal chest CT and paraneoplastic antibody panel do not rule this out, as it is often associated with non-Hodgkin lymphoma, Castleman disease, or thymoma which may not yet be radiographically obvious or have negative specific antibody serology.
